target_customer: Independent bands and labels paying for promotion, and music listeners who stream the free radio
problem: Independent artists had few ways to reach listeners, while internet radio was dominated by licensed major label catalogs. Earbits let artists pay for extra plays to a matched audience.
business_model: Free ad-supported artist-curated internet radio with pay-per-play promotion sold to bands and labels
product_category: Internet radio, music discovery, artist promotion marketplace

founders.name: Joey Flores
previous_startups: Led business development at an earlier startup and left after a buyout (not named in TNW)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has worked in startups since 1998; later head of marketing at SafetyWing. Drummer.

founders.name: Yotam Rosenbaum
education: Berklee College of Music, composition degree
founders.background_notes: Musician and composer for TV and commercials per The Next Web, 2011. Later led First Peak Ventures per YC page.

founders.name: Benjamin Bryant
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as founder and VP Technology.

technical_complexity.rationale: Streaming radio apps and a bidding system for plays; licensing and catalog building were harder than the engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Direct deals with independent labels and artists gave a catalog but nothing stopped larger services from offering independent music promotion.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large streamers absorbed independent music discovery; Earbits ran short of funds and announced a shutdown in 2014, returned online funded by You42 and was acquired by it.

market_need_then: Independent artists wanted exposure and spent on promotion, and May 2011 coverage described an audience gap for artist-focused radio against crowded major label services. Spend per band was small.

branding.domain_note: Used earbits.com, which now redirects to you42.com after the acquisition.

identity.voice_and_tone: Musician-led, indie friendly; founders are drummers and one a Berklee composer.

branding.brand_signature: Pitch as Google AdWords for music
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by The Next Web, Hypebot, Gizmodo and SoCal Tech; ran a SXSW channel and a Topspin merch tie-in per Hypebot headlines; its shutdown and revival got press.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized in music tech press and by indie artists, but no evidence of a large consumer following or brand driven growth.

pivots.to: Added social currency letting fans unlock on-demand features, with iOS and Android apps
pivots.why: Not stated in sources opened; seen in 2013 coverage headlines

outcome_analysis: Earbits built an indie focused radio with pay-per-play promotion and reported about 1.7 million dollars raised in total per Hypebot. It announced a shutdown in 2014 after running out of funding, was revived by a partner later named as You42 and was acquired by it, announced in September 2015 with terms undisclosed. The market had large streaming competitors and small per-artist budgets, so growth capital never arrived.
notes: Website earbits.com redirects to you42.com.
